item.title: ADBC vs Arrow Flight SQL vs JDBC in 2026: Stop Copying Rows Between Your Database and Your Pipeline
item.description: Every analytics pipeline built on a classic driver pays the same tax, and almost nobody measures it. A query returns rows: the driver materialises one Python object (or one JVM object, or one Go struct) per row, your code converts those rows into a columnar frame, and then the frame is serialised again to move to the next process. For a 50-million-row scan, that is three full transpositions of the data — the query itself is often the fast part.
